disease_label_per_paper: Acute epididymo-orchitis complicated with abscesses in testis and seminal vesicles
presentation_summary: 28-year-old married man first sought care for painful scrotal swelling lasting one week and was diagnosed clinically with bilateral epididymo-orchitis.
Initial urinalysis showed 12-15 pus cells per high-power field and he was prescribed ciprofloxacin and analgesics.

Five days later he developed stepping scrotal pain, worsening swelling, fever to 40 degC, chills, unease, anorexia, and nausea; he was treated with sulbactam/cefoperazone and diclofenac without improvement.
During clinical deterioration fever reached 41.5 degC with vomiting, insomnia, and exhaustion; labs showed WBC 24.3 x 10^9/L, neutrophils 88%, and CRP 96 mg/dL in the source report.

Digital rectal examination showed tender cystic structures over the prostate, and ultrasound/TRUS showed markedly dilated seminal vesicles with echogenic contents suggesting abscesses and a small midline prostatic utricle cyst.

At Alexandria Main University Hospital he denied genital trauma, diabetes, tuberculosis, urethral discharge, sexually transmitted disease, extramarital relations, and previous similar conditions; he had seven years of primary infertility with low semen volume and azoospermia.

Definitive presentation showed tachycardia, low blood pressure, fever 40.5 degC, suprapubic and bilateral inguinal tenderness/rigidity, erythematous swollen excoriated scrotum, tender indurated scrotum, epididymides not separately palpable from testes, tender indurated spermatic cords, and enlarged tender seminal vesicles on DRE.
Pelvic MRI showed markedly dilated seminal vesicles with abnormal signal and a suspicious lower-pole left testicular fluid collection suggesting impending abscess formation.
